title: Prove full retained boxes for rational Gram factorizations
body:
For any rational three-column Gram factorization `M=P P^T` whose canonical ties are all nonempty, this package proves a full retained directed anchor box, for arbitrary row count. Canonical normalization need not preserve `P=Q`: the proof identifies the original tied sets using a common global scaling, splits the even-tied rows by an odd-coordinate product modulo four, and applies the inherited two-block/odd-middle labels.

For general rational factors it also proves simultaneous retention of every odd-tied row and every matched two-bit row with diagonal valuation `gamma+1`. A four-row matched-anchor example with box three shows why higher cancellation cannot simply be admitted. Aaron Wang's existing symmetric positive-definite three-row core is retained as a separate control: symmetry of the matrix does not replace the hypothesis on the supplied factors.

Only `research/fstar-gram-full-box/` is added. The package includes the complete written proof, exact normalization and witness checker, unchanged source-pinned definition oracle, receipts, attribution and open questions. It credits the original F-star/canonical-anchor framework, PR3409/3420/3445 labeling transfers and PR3454's finite Gram construction. Same-session AI review is not independent human acceptance or formal verification.

Validation on CPython 3.12.15:

- Both registered replay commands pass, including `-I -O -B -Werror`.
- All 96 admitted modulo-four types and 9,216 ordered pairs; eight Gram fixture families; three 100-row asymmetric families; partial retention and nine failure controls.
- Exact maximum-box searches only on four-, three- and two-row boundary cases. Explicit positive maximum witnesses receive a separate literal check.
- Metadata, all eight committed package files and source history pass. The frozen oracle matches its pinned original Git bytes.
- Fork main synced to canonical `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`; contribution branch rebased.

The unrestricted asymmetric twelve-line target remains open. This is a scoped algebraic proof supported by finite checks, not native supplier admission, a complete multiplication theorem or a new kappa. Selected frontier unchanged.

Coordination: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1317#discussioncomment-19015031

Authored by Sagar Thakrar with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including separate proof, executable-check and adversarial-review agents.
